neighbours.label: the rest of a word after a split-off 'sh' piece (sh|ied, sh|ying, sh|irked, sh|abby)
fire: The pony kept shying at every gate along the lane.
He shied a pebble across the pond and laughed.
Nobody liked him for shirking the night shifts.
They sat on the porch shucking oysters until dark.
The engine was shunted onto a siding near the mill.
She kept shooing the hens away from the kitchen door.
The curtains hung shabbily over a cracked window.
The old dancer shimmied across the stage to loud applause.
quiet: The pony kept balking at every gate along the lane.
He flicked a pebble across the pond and laughed.
Nobody liked him for dodging the night duties.
They sat on the porch prising oysters open until dark.
The engine was diverted onto a siding near the mill.
The girl kept waving the hens away from the kitchen door.
The curtains hung limply over a cracked window.
The old dancer glided across the stage to loud applause.

notes: Card flags the pole broad (2.0% of tokens reach 0.1 of max) and gate-closed; peaks 'ipped', 'ipping', 'shine', 'ying' and Arabic/Cyrillic pieces after a sh-sound letter. The - pole is the whole tokens ' ship'/' shipping', so the unit separates whole ship words from spelled-out sh- words. Probes: shying 0.86, shied 0.88, shirked/shucked/shunned 0.64, shabby 0.61, shined 0.56; no sh- word 0.02-0.09. Near misses swap in rare verbs that do not start with sh.
